notes:
Default middleware profile shipped in the package (HoUnityTools/Editor/FaceTracking/Profiles/).
Warudo cannot read the package: COPY this file into the plugin sandbox (the node's "open folder"
button opens exactly that directory) and edit it there.

>>> THE OUTPUT SIDE IS A TRANSITIONAL ARTIFACT. <<<
The end state is ANIMATIONS, not ARKit blend shapes: one animation expresses one state, the
animations have no standard naming, and WHICH axes become 2D blend trees is the author's call
per model. The 52 `ARKit/<name>` output rows below exist only so the whole chain can be driven
with an off-the-shelf model before those animations exist. When they do exist, the output rows
become "canonical name -> author's parameter name" and NOTHING ELSE CHANGES: the interface
between the two layers is still one Dictionary<string,float>.
See docs/FACE_TRACKING_WORKFLOW.md section 2.1.
The INPUT side (wire name -> canonical name) is long-lived and does NOT go away with that change.

WHAT IT DOES
  wire name -> canonical name for the two dialects we have actually observed, plus
  canonical -> output (52 ARKit pass-through + the 6 reserved Head names).

WHAT IT IS NOT
  It is NOT calibrated. VBridger's own input-curve store is 68 rows of identity (0->0 / 1->1),
  and its preset numbers describe VBridger's own channel set, not ARKit pass-through. Per
  docs/VTS_FACE_PARAMETER_SPACES.md: the expression value, the saved default and the model's
  final neutral need not be equal. Calibration is per-actor/per-device work and belongs here,
  in YOUR copy.

OVERRIDE RULE
  Same-name multiple rows = LAST row wins, and a row whose wire is missing does NOT fall back
  (that cell is simply 0). So the two shape dialects WOULD fight over the same canonical name.
  Only use one device at a time: delete the rows you do not need. Keeping both is safe only
  because "missing wire" rows stay frozen -- but it is much easier to misread.

UNITS
  Head rotation is degrees; head position units are NOT calibrated (raw phone values pass
  through). Both are clamped to the curve range, which is why those rows carry +/-180.

CALIBRATION STARTING POINTS (measured from VBridger AdvancedARKit V3, seconds, its "smooth"):
  jawOpen 0.10 | mouth* 0.10 | eyeLook* 0.10 | eyeBlink+eyeWide 0.10 | browInnerUp 0.32
  browOuterUp-browDown 0.40 | cheekPuff / tongueOut / eyeSquint 0 (no filtering)
  Add {"kind":"smooth","seconds":0.1} to that row's modifiers.
